name: Indo-Gangetic Plain
climate: Humid subtropical (Cwa) in the east, semi-arid in the west
temp: Hot summers to 45 °C; cool winters with fog
soils: Alluvial soil; Saline and alkaline soil (usar) in patches
landscape: Flat plains of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra; khadar and bhangar terraces
vegetation: Mostly farmland; remnant sal forest and terai grassland
wildlife: Blackbuck, Nilgai, Sarus crane, Indian peafowl, Gharial
crops: Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane, Potato, Mustard / rapeseed, Mango
people: Home to about 600 million people, one of the densest farm populations on Earth
threats: Groundwater depletion, stubble-burning smog, floods, soil salinity
summary: India's grain bowl, built by Himalayan rivers that renew the soil with silt.

name: Punjab plains
landscape: Flat doab lands between five rivers
wildlife: Indian peafowl, Black francolin
people: Green Revolution heartland; Sikh and Punjabi farming culture
threats: Falling water tables of ~0.5–1 m a year; pesticide overuse
summary: The 'land of five rivers', fed by the world's largest canal network.

name: Thar and Marwar
landscape: Sand dunes, rocky plains, salt lakes (Sambhar)
vegetation: Khejri, rohida, ker and grass scrub
wildlife: Chinkara, Great Indian bustard, Indian desert cat, Desert monitor
crops: Pearl millet (bajra), Moth bean, Cluster bean (guar), Mustard / rapeseed
people: Rajasthani pastoral and trading communities; Bishnoi conservationists
threats: Desertification, solar and wind farm expansion, power lines killing bustards
summary: One of the most densely populated deserts in the world.

name: Rann of Kutch and Kathiawar
landscape: Seasonal salt desert, Banni grassland, Gir hills
vegetation: Thorn scrub, mangroves, Gir dry deciduous forest
wildlife: Indian wild ass, Greater flamingo, Asiatic lion, Caracal
people: Rabari and Maldhari herders; famous textile crafts
summary: A white salt desert that floods each monsoon, beside the last home of Asiatic lions.

name: Western Ghats
climate: Tropical monsoon (Am) on the west; rain shadow to the east
soils: Laterite soil; Red soil; Forest and mountain soil
landscape: Escarpment, sholas, plateaus, Nilgiri and Anamalai hills
wildlife: Lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr, Purple frog, Great hornbill, Malabar giant squirrel, Bengal tiger, Asian elephant
crops: Tea, Coffee (arabica), Black pepper, Cardamom, Rubber, Coconut
people: Kodava, Toda, Kurumba and many forest communities
summary: A UNESCO biodiversity hotspot older than the Himalaya, catching the monsoon for peninsular India.

name: Deccan Plateau
soils: Black cotton soil (regur); Red soil; Vertisols
landscape: Basalt traps in the northwest, granite tors in the south
vegetation: Dry deciduous forest and thorn scrub
wildlife: Blackbuck, Indian wolf, Great Indian bustard, Sloth bear
crops: Cotton, Sorghum (jowar), Soybean, Pigeon pea (arhar/tur), Groundnut, Grape, Pomegranate
people: Marathi, Kannada and Telugu farming heartlands
summary: The ancient core of peninsular India, built on lava and granite.

name: Malwa and Bundelkhand
landscape: Undulating basalt plateau and rocky Vindhyan uplands
wildlife: Bengal tiger, Leopard, Indian wolf, Gharial
people: Historic kingdoms of Malwa, Chandelas of Khajuraho
summary: Central India's soybean and wheat belt.

name: Chota Nagpur Plateau
wildlife: Asian elephant, Sloth bear, Leopard
people: Santhal, Munda, Ho and Oraon Adivasi homeland
summary: India's mineral heart and Adivasi homeland.

name: Eastern Ghats and Odisha
landscape: Broken hill ranges, Chilika lagoon, Mahanadi delta
wildlife: Olive ridley turtle, Irrawaddy dolphin, Indian golden gecko, Jerdon's courser
summary: Older, eroded hills along the Bay of Bengal.

name: Himalaya (western)
landscape: Shiwaliks, Lesser and Greater Himalaya, glaciers
vegetation: Chir pine, oak, deodar, alpine meadows
wildlife: Snow leopard, Himalayan tahr, Western tragopan, Himalayan monal, Musk deer
people: Pahari, Garhwali, Kumaoni and Himachali hill cultures
summary: The young western arc of the Himalaya, source of the Ganga and Yamuna.

name: Himalaya (eastern) and Northeast
climate: Humid subtropical to alpine; among the wettest places
soils: Forest and mountain soil; Laterite soil
landscape: Sikkim and Arunachal Himalaya, Khasi and Naga hills, Brahmaputra valley
wildlife: Red panda, Hoolock gibbon, Clouded leopard, Indian rhinoceros, Golden langur, Great hornbill
people: Over 200 tribes including Naga, Khasi, Apatani, Mishing
summary: India's biodiversity crown and one of its wettest regions.

name: Ladakh and Spiti
wildlife: Snow leopard, Tibetan wild ass, Black-necked crane, Tibetan antelope
summary: A high cold desert behind the Himalaya, farmed by glacier-fed channels.

name: Sundarbans and Bengal delta
soils: Alluvial soil; Saline and alkaline soil (usar)
wildlife: Bengal tiger, Saltwater crocodile, Fishing cat, Masked finfoot
summary: The world's largest mangrove forest.

name: Kerala and Konkan coast
soils: Laterite soil; Alluvial soil; Peaty and marshy soil
wildlife: Smooth-coated otter, Malabar pied hornbill
crops: Coconut, Rice, Black pepper, Cashew, Mango
summary: A wet green coast of backwaters and spices.

name: Coromandel coast and Kaveri delta
climate: Tropical wet and dry; northeast-monsoon rain
landscape: Deltas of the Kaveri, Krishna and Godavari
wildlife: Olive ridley turtle, Painted stork
summary: The 'rice bowl' of South India.

name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
wildlife: Nicobar pigeon, Saltwater crocodile, Andaman woodpecker, Leatherback turtle
summary: Rainforest islands home to some of the world's last isolated peoples.

name: Tibetan Plateau
landscape: The highest plateau, ringed by the Himalaya and Kunlun
wildlife: Wild yak, Tibetan antelope, Snow leopard, Plateau pika, Kiang
summary: The 'Third Pole' and the water tower of Asia.

name: Mongolian steppe and Gobi
wildlife: Przewalski's horse, Mongolian gazelle, Wild Bactrian camel, Saker falcon

name: North China Plain

summary: One of the most intensively farmed plains on Earth.

name: Loess Plateau

name: Yangtze basin

name: Mekong basin

name: Borneo

summary: An ancient rainforest island losing ground to plantations.

name: Siberian taiga
wildlife: Siberian tiger, Sable, Reindeer, Moose
summary: The largest forest on Earth.

name: Arabian Peninsula
landscape: Rub' al Khali, Hejaz and Hajar mountains
wildlife: Arabian oryx, Arabian leopard, Sand cat
summary: The largest peninsula and one of the driest.

name: Fertile Crescent and Mesopotamia
wildlife: Persian leopard, Wild goat
summary: The birthplace of agriculture and writing.

name: Central Asian deserts and steppe
wildlife: Saiga, Goitered gazelle, Corsac fox
people: Silk Road cities of Samarkand and Bukhara
summary: The Silk Road heartland, transformed by Soviet cotton.

name: Sahara
countries: Algeria; Libya; Egypt; Mali; Niger; Chad; Sudan; Mauritania
temp: Extreme heat by day, cold nights
landscape: Ergs, regs, Ahaggar and Tibesti mountains
wildlife: Fennec fox, Addax, Dromedary camel, Horned viper
summary: The largest hot desert, green only 6,000 years ago.

name: Sahel
countries: Senegal; Mali; Burkina Faso; Niger; Chad; Sudan
landscape: Flat plains between the Sahara and savanna
wildlife: Scimitar oryx, Patas monkey
summary: A belt of recurrent drought and remarkable restoration.

name: Nile Valley and delta
wildlife: Nile crocodile, Sacred ibis
threats: Lost silt after Aswan; sea-level rise in the delta
summary: A green ribbon that fed one of the first civilisations.

name: Ethiopian Highlands
landscape: Plateaus above 2,000 m, Simien and Bale mountains
wildlife: Gelada, Ethiopian wolf, Walia ibex, Mountain nyala
people: One of the oldest Christian kingdoms
summary: The 'roof of Africa', birthplace of coffee and teff.

name: Great Rift Valley
wildlife: Lesser flamingo, African lion, Giraffe
summary: Where Africa is splitting and where humans evolved.

name: Serengeti–Mara ecosystem
wildlife: Blue wildebeest, Plains zebra, African lion, Cheetah, Spotted hyena
summary: Home of the greatest land migration.

name: Congo Basin

name: Kalahari and Okavango

name: Namib Desert
landscape: Red dunes up to 300 m, Skeleton Coast
wildlife: Fog-basking beetle, Gemsbok, Brown hyena

name: Cape Floristic Region
wildlife: King protea, Cape sugarbird, Bontebok
summary: The smallest and richest of the world's plant kingdoms.

name: Madagascar
landscape: Central highlands, eastern rainforest, western dry forest, spiny forest

people: Malagasy of Austronesian and African descent

name: Mediterranean Basin
temp: Hot dry summers, mild wet winters
wildlife: Iberian lynx, Mediterranean monk seal, Hermann's tortoise
people: Cradle of Greek and Roman civilisation

name: Alps

name: Pontic–Caspian steppe and black earth

name: Scandinavia and Fennoscandia

summary: Land scraped by Ice Age glaciers.

name: British Isles uplands
wildlife: Red deer, Golden eagle
summary: Treeless moors largely created by people.

name: Amazon rainforest region
wildlife: Jaguar, Giant otter, Harpy eagle, Hyacinth macaw, Pink river dolphin, Brazil nut
summary: The largest rainforest and river system.

name: Cerrado
wildlife: Maned wolf, Giant anteater, Hyacinth macaw
summary: The most biodiverse savanna, now Brazil's farm frontier.

name: Pantanal
wildlife: Jaguar, Capybara, Yacare caiman, Jabiru, Hyacinth macaw
summary: The world's largest tropical wetland.

name: Andes

wildlife: Andean condor, Vicuña, Spectacled bear, Mountain tapir
summary: The longest continental range, home of potatoes and the Inca.

name: Atacama and Altiplano
wildlife: Vicuña, Andean flamingo, Chinchilla

name: Pampas

name: Patagonia
wildlife: Guanaco, Puma, Darwin's rhea, Huemul

name: Mesoamerican highlands and Yucatán
wildlife: Jaguar, Resplendent quetzal, Ocellated turkey
summary: Where maize was domesticated and the Maya built cities.

name: Great Plains
wildlife: American bison, Pronghorn, Prairie dog, Greater prairie-chicken
summary: The North American breadbasket, site of the Dust Bowl.

name: Rocky Mountains
wildlife: Grizzly bear, Gray wolf, Elk, Bighorn sheep, Mountain goat
summary: The backbone of North America.

name: Sonoran and Mojave deserts
wildlife: Gila monster, Desert tortoise, Roadrunner
summary: The hottest deserts of North America.

name: Canadian Shield and boreal
wildlife: Moose, Canada lynx, Wolverine, Common loon
summary: The ancient rocky core of North America.

name: Arctic tundra
wildlife: Polar bear, Arctic fox, Muskox, Snowy owl, Reindeer
summary: The treeless top of the world.

name: Australian Outback
wildlife: Red kangaroo, Thorny devil, Dingo, Emu
people: Aboriginal nations with 65,000 years of culture
summary: A vast red interior of ancient landscapes.

name: Great Dividing Range and east coast
wildlife: Koala, Platypus, Superb lyrebird, Lumholtz's tree-kangaroo

name: New Zealand
wildlife: Kiwi (North Island brown), Kea, Kakapo, Tuatara

name: New Guinea
wildlife: Goodfellow's tree-kangaroo, Victoria crowned pigeon, Southern cassowary, Birds-of-paradise

name: Antarctica
wildlife: Emperor penguin, Adélie penguin, Weddell seal

name: Vidarbha and Marathwada
wildlife: Bengal tiger, Sloth bear, Indian wolf

crops: Rice, Jute, Wheat, Lychee, Fox nut (makhana)

name: Assam and Brahmaputra valley

wildlife: Indian rhinoceros, Asian elephant, Wild water buffalo, Pygmy hog, Bengal florican

name: Kashmir valley
wildlife: Hangul, Himalayan black bear, Snow leopard
summary: A lake-filled valley famous for saffron.

name: Uttarakhand and Kumaon
landscape: Garhwal and Kumaon Himalaya, Ganga headwaters
wildlife: Himalayan monal, Snow leopard, Bengal tiger (Corbett)

name: Meghalaya plateau
landscape: Khasi, Garo and Jaintia hills; caves
wildlife: Hoolock gibbon, Clouded leopard
summary: Home of the wettest places and living root bridges.

name: Iranian Plateau
landscape: Salt deserts ringed by Zagros and Alborz
wildlife: Persian leopard, Asiatic cheetah, Onager
summary: A high dry plateau watered by ancient qanats.

name: Anatolia
landscape: Central plateau, Taurus and Pontic mountains
wildlife: Brown bear, Wild goat
people: Hittite, Greek, Byzantine and Ottoman heritage
summary: A land bridge between Asia and Europe.

name: Levant
landscape: Coastal plain, Jordan Rift, Dead Sea
wildlife: Nubian ibex, Mountain gazelle
summary: A narrow corridor where early farming and religions began.

name: Japanese archipelago
wildlife: Japanese macaque, Sika deer, Red-crowned crane
summary: A mountainous volcanic chain farmed in terraces.

name: Korean Peninsula
wildlife: Red-crowned crane, Siberian tiger (historic)
summary: A mountainous peninsula with a DMZ wildlife refuge.

name: Indochina highlands
wildlife: Saola, Red-shanked douc, Asian elephant
summary: Mountains with newly discovered mammals.

name: Philippine archipelago
wildlife: Philippine eagle, Philippine tarsier, Tamaraw

name: Sumatra and Java
wildlife: Sumatran tiger, Sumatran orangutan, Javan rhinoceros, Sumatran elephant

name: Hindu Kush and Karakoram
wildlife: Markhor, Snow leopard, Himalayan brown bear

landscape: Atlas ranges between the sea and the Sahara

wildlife: Sable antelope, African wild dog, African elephant
people: Bemba, Shona and other farming peoples

name: Albertine Rift and Virunga
wildlife: Mountain gorilla, Golden monkey, Chimpanzee
summary: Africa's richest region for vertebrates.

name: Karoo
wildlife: Springbok, Ostrich
summary: A semi-desert rich in fossils and succulents.

name: Iberian Peninsula
wildlife: Iberian lynx, Spanish imperial eagle
people: Celtic, Roman, Moorish and Iberian heritage
summary: Europe's hottest and driest peninsula.

name: Carpathians

name: Balkans

name: Appalachians and eastern forests

name: Mississippi basin and Corn Belt
wildlife: White-tailed deer
summary: The world's most productive maize region.

name: California and Central Valley
wildlife: California condor, Giant sequoia, Coast redwood
